analysis.title: Round trip: Gone baby gone, AI momentum trade erases all YTD gains
key_insights: The GS High Beta Momentum Pair has erased all YTD gains. It was up about 70% at its peak in June and is now back to zero in October.

GS trading desk: Thursday saw another leg lower in past winners, with a broad AI/Semis selloff as the costs-versus-returns debate was reinforced by META's earnings. It was the worst performance of AI Beneficiaries vs Top 500 ex AI since Deepseek Monday.

The SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over the last 9 sessions (since Mon 10/12), the biggest 9-day stretch of underperformance in 20+ years. The SOX is now testing its 200-DMA for the first time since June 2025.
Unconstrained Momentum is having its worst drawdown since the GFC, excluding the Covid period.
Momentum factor exposure has fallen to its lowest level since late June 2025 but is still elevated vs history, at the 73rd percentile on a 5-year basis.
GS Prime: Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.1 pts month to date to 49.4%, the 1st percentile over 1 year and the 4th percentile over 3 years.
Short leverage has risen sharply and is near 5-year highs (99th percentile). Long leverage has also risen to the 94th percentile.
The aggregate long/short ratio for Global AI stocks is in the 6th percentile vs the past year. Net leverage is still fairly high on a longer view.
Systematic funds' short book exposure rose sharply in October, but the level is not unprecedented for the year (UBS chart, 5-year percentile).
Low vol is back as a favoured factor in October, after a long period when the trade was 'the riskier the better'.

Exposure to profitability is at a 5-year high. GS trading desk says its quality index (sector/industry/factor neutral) is up about 20% in 3 months, driven by underperformance of the short leg (lower quality).

sector_views.rationale: Broad AI/Semis selloff, SOX down 13% vs S&P 500 over 9 sessions and testing its 200-DMA. Debate over AI costs versus returns reinforced by META earnings.

earnings_insights: META's earnings reinforced the costs-versus-returns debate on AI spending, according to the GS trading desk, triggering a leg lower in AI/Semis names on Thursday.
risk_factors: Positioning signals conflict. Some charts suggest the AI momentum unwind is not over, while others suggest it is done.
Momentum factor exposure is still elevated (73rd percentile 5-year), leaving room for further de-risking.
Short leverage near 5-year highs and rising systematic shorts could add pressure or set up a squeeze.
The costs-versus-returns debate on AI capex continues to weigh on the group after META's earnings.
The SOX is testing its 200-DMA, and a break could extend the selloff.

tension_points.bull_case: Signals suggest the washout may be done: the AI long/short ratio is at the 6th percentile, momentum exposure is at its lowest since June 2025, and fundamental L/S net leverage is at the 1st percentile.
tension_points.bear_case: Momentum exposure is still at the 73rd percentile, short leverage is near 99th percentile with systematic shorts rising, and net leverage on AI stocks is still high on a longer view, so the pain may not be over.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The SOX breaking below its 200-DMA, which it is testing for the first time since June 2025.
